title: Other translations: Ada to C++, Fortran modernisation, MATLAB to/from C++ for embedded targets
subtitle: Discussion only. No fixture, scanner, or skill exists for these three; this is how the same method would apply
footer: Tool names are for discussion; verify status and licences with your administrator (integrations/tool-approval-status.md).

slides.title: Same method, four stages
bullets: Discover: inventory, candidate dependency graph, dynamic / vendor / target-only markers, port / wrap / retain / unreadable, repo map, backlog
Pack: one bounded context file per unit, leaf-first, with a result contract
Migrate one unit with a skill that ends in bench_compare.py on recorded vectors
Track and report; rescan as the estate changes
Adding a language = a scanner emitting the same dependency-map.json + a fixture + expected/ + a golden stage; prompt_pack and pipeline_run work unchanged

slides.title: Ada to C++
left: Ranges, subtypes, discriminated records; generics; representation clauses
Tasking and protected objects; interrupt handlers
SPARK contracts and certification evidence tied to the original
right: libadalang / GNAT parse Ada from Python; GNAT Pro CCG generates C as a product; no maintained OSS Ada-to-C++ translator
Scanner: with / use, spec vs body, tasks, protected types, generics, pragmas, Interfaces.C
Tasking, rep clauses, interrupt handlers -> retain / wrap first; proof per subprogram on vectors

slides.title: Fortran modernisation
left: Fixed-form F77: COMMON, EQUIVALENCE, computed GOTO, implicit typing
COMMON makes dependencies a data-flow problem, not a call graph
Numerics: precision, evaluation order, compiler flags define 'equivalent'
right: fparser, LFortran (AST / ASR), fable / cctbx (F77 to C++); f2py wraps instead of translating - often step one
Scanner: program units, CALL graph, COMMON and MODULE membership, INCLUDE, implicit typing, GOTO, I/O units
COMMON- and I/O-heavy units wrap first; numerical kernels port; tolerance per column in bench_compare.py

slides.title: MATLAB to / from C++ for embedded algorithms
left: /matlab-to-code --target c, proven on vectors (26 vectors, Python and C exact)
/repo-discovery for the MATLAB tree; /bring-your-firmware + host harness for the C side
MATLAB to C on a host, end to end
right: C++ output; MATLAB Coder / Embedded Coder review as a fixture (licence); fixed-point conversion
Reverse direction (C++ algorithm to MATLAB for simulation)

slides.title: FedRAMP / CUI environment notes
bullets: Everything here runs offline from the working tree: standard-library Python, optional C compiler, optional lvkit
Viewing public repositories was confirmed; cloning was not - the README describes the Download-ZIP path
Any tool named on these slides goes through the administrator's approval first
No claim is made that any service is inside a FedRAMP boundary

slides.text: Related examples, not demonstrated lanes. The method carries over; the scanner, fixture, and proof for each would still have to be built.
